name: String argument index processing
goal: I created a program where I can add commands using a dynamic format. Using a unique command, I can add commands on runtime using "!command add {command name} {command text}". When the command is then invoked ("!{command name}"), the command text will show and parameters are filled. Example: "!command add cookie You are given a ${0} cookie!". "!cookie sweet" will then result in "You are given a sweet cookie!". The variable ${0} is replaced by the first word after the command name. When a command is added, some variable indices can accidentally be skipped, especially the first one: 0. "!command add cookie ${4} is given a ${1} cookie""!cookie sweet Marco" will then produce "undefined is given a Marco cookie". The algorithm must refactor the initial command to order the indices correctly. "${4} is given a ${1} cookie" will be refactored to "${1} is given a ${0} cookie", as non existing indices are skipped.

approach.text:
I started by breaking down the algorithm in sections, to solve each section one by one:

Input:
"${4} is given a ${1} cookie"
1. Get the highest index: 4
2. Loop through indices while highest index is not reached and replace them with lowest index
1st iteration: "${4} is given a ${0} cookie".
2nd iteration: "${1} is given a ${0} cookie".
After the breakdown was made, I created a test project separate from the program to make development easier. I tested the code with test data, and after a bit of debugging, it worked out well.

normalLearnings: I can create breakdowns of complex problems to smaller simple problems.
